# dsh-subagent-gemini

> **发布状态：暂未发布到 npm / DSH 插件市场。**
> Gemini CLI 目前尚未提供 Gemini 4，且本插件需要用户自备 Gemini API key 才能完成端到端验证；
>

在验证通过前不提交市场收录，避免把未经验证的插件放给用户。代码、测试与 CI 均已就绪，验证后可发布。
>
> 想用 Gemini 4 请安装 `dsh-subagent-antigravity`。
English | 中文

Adds a **Gemini subagent** to DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a parent session can call
`subagent_gemini` to

run a Google Gemini CLI coding agent in a **separate process**
inside the parent workspace, let it

edit files and run commands on its own, and
get only the final answer back.

The shape is the same as the official Codex subagent (`subagent_codex`) and the
community Cursor sub
agent (`cursor_code`):

- **Fresh process, fresh session** — every delegation spawns a new `gemini --acp`;
- **Final answer

only** — the child's thoughts, tool calls and stderr never enter the parent conversation;
- **One ta
sk per run** — no follow-up input or continuation (use the native `subagent`/`fork` backends for tho

se);
- **Safe diagnostics** — failures report fixed stage/category facts, never stderr, paths or cre
Safe diagnostics** — failures report fixed stage/category facts, never stderr, paths or credentials.
> Community plugin; not affiliated with Google. Gemini CLI is Google's official CLI — this plugin on
ly drives it from DSH.

## Credentials (important)
Gemini CLI needs its own credential. **Google account browser login (OAuth) no longer works**: Googl

e retired
the individual Gemini Code Assist OAuth client for Gemini CLI, and the CLI reports
*"This

client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals"*.
Use an **API key** instead:

1. Create a key at <https://aistudio.google.com/apikey>;
2. Store it where Gemini CLI looks (no plug
in config required):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Gemini CLI loads `~/.gemini/.env` automatically. Environment variables also work:

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` — Gemini Developer API;
- `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true` + `GOOGLE_API_KEY` — V

ertex AI;
- `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_GCA=true` — Google Code Assist license.
To pass variables to the child explicitly, use the plugin's `env` config (see below). The plugin nev

er reads,
logs or returns secret values.
## Usage
The model calls it like any other delegation tool:

- `description` — 3–5 word task name shown in the subagent list;
- `prompt` — a **self-contained** t
ask; the child cannot see the parent conversation, so include paths, constraints and acceptance crit
the child cannot see the parent conversation, so include paths, constraints and acceptance criteria.
When the run finishes the parent receives a completion notice with Gemini's final answer or a safe f

ailure
diagnostic. The child's tool traffic and reasoning stay out of the parent session.

## Security and permissions
- `permission: allow` means **unattended**: the child may edit workspace files and run commands with

out a human
approval prompt. That is what makes delegated coding tasks possible; use it in trusted w

orkspaces and review
`git diff` afterwards.
- `--skip-trust` trusts the parent workspace for the chi

ld session only, so a delegation never stalls on an
interactive trust prompt.
- The child is a separ

ate process with its own credential environment: DSH's subprocess seam scrubs credential-like
variab

les from the parent environment; only variables in `env` are forwarded.
- No telemetry. No credentia
l is read, logged or returned by this plugin; the key is managed by Gemini CLI itself.
## Compatibility and development
- Depends on the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-acp@0.2.1-rc.2`, so protocol work tracks the of

ficial backend;
- Unit tests: `npm test` (32 cases: config normalization, executable discovery, cred

mentations: the official Codex subagent (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex`) and the official ACP
bac
kend (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-acp`); all three share the same `ctx.subagents` contract.
